key_insight: A controllable 4D cardiac MRI generator separates anatomy from motion to create anatomically consistent synthetic sequences for data augmentation.
clinical_relevance: Synthetic 4D MRI can help improve downstream cardiac segmentation performance, especially when real annotated data are limited or scans vary across vendors.
method: Semi-supervised VAE learns compact anatomical latents and predicts aligned segmentation masks.
Static latent diffusion models subject-specific anatomy from clinical priors such as diagnosis and volume measures.
A second diffusion model adds residual motion to keep the full 4D sequence temporally coherent.
evidence_signal: Across multiple datasets, the model showed strong controllability of anatomy (Pearson r > 0.8) and temporal coherence (FVD = 288.08), and synthetic augmentation improved nnU-Net segmentation results.
watch_item: Synthetic data quality and benefit may depend on the target scanner/domain, so cross-vendor validation and careful integration into training pipelines remain important.
paper_title: Anatomy-Guided Residual Motion Diffusion for Controllable 4D Cardiac MRI Synthesis
